subject: [Velox] High error + p99 latency after model v3.1 quant rollout / Exec attention
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@velox.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: support@velox.ai
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 17:23:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate + p99 latency after model v3.1 quant rollout

Jonas —

We pushed Redwood model v3.1 with the new 4-bit quant profile to production around 14:00 PT today. Within ~30 minutes our API error rate spiked from 0.3% -> 4.6% and p99 latency jumped from ~210ms to ~1.2s. We rolled a quick fallback to the previous variant at 16:20 and saw latency return toward baseline, but the customer-facing incidents already started.

I attached the support logs and a small KV-cache trace. We rely heavily on short prompt caching; curious if the new quant kernels are causing decode stalls or additional KV thrash. Our SLO is 99.9% < 500ms so this is a production-impacting event for us.

Can you route this to engineering ASAP and advise next steps? We may need credits or SLA remediation for impacted customers.

—Elena

Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 17:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + p99 latency after model v3.1 quant rollout

Thanks Elena — and thanks for the logs. I've started an internal triage. Initial notes:

- Confirmed timeline matches our rollout telemetry: v3.1 (q4b-econ) served from us-west-2 pool at 14:02 PT, traffic shift completed by 14:08.
- The KV trace shows repeated cache invalidations for short prompts (many prefix hits followed by cache misses).
- Error signatures in the logs are 502/504 framed around decoder hang timeouts.

Immediate ask: can you share a sanitized prompt sample that reproduces the high latency? If you prefer, we can accept a short collection in the shared Drive link you sent.

We are spinning up a debug debug-build that increases decode logging and will evaluate a quick rollback plan if we see a deterministic kernel/path causing stalls. Rishi — can you assign an SRE to run a quick profile on the us-west-2 serving pool? Monica/Marissa — pinging you for visibility; this looks like an SLO exposure and Velox is asking about credits.

I will follow up with a proposed timeline for an incident call within 45 minutes.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0987
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, elena.soto@velox.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + p99 latency after model v3.1 quant rollout

Jonas — thanks. I've started an SRE job to capture perf profiles and will look specifically at:

1) Kernel selection path for q4b-econ on A100 nodes — making sure the fast-path isn't accidentally disabled for short sequences.
2) KV-cache eviction churn metrics + correlation with throttling on the frontend.
3) Per-request decode stalls and whether batch size heuristics changed when the model variant swapped.

Preliminary hypothesis: the quant profile introduced slightly different block sizes that interact badly with our compact KV layout, producing more cache misses under short prompt distributions. That increases per-request work and triggers decode timeouts at high concurrency.

If the hypothesis holds we have two quick mitigation options: (a) pin Velox to v3.0 variant for 24–48h while we roll an alternate quant profile, or (b) apply a serving-side patch to adjust KV prefetch thresholds for q4b-econ. Option (a) is fastest and avoids risk; option (b) reduces churn but needs 2–3h engineering work and can be tested on canary first.

We'll aim to confirm in the incident call.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Serving & Reliability | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 03 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: [EXEC] Velox incident — request for credits and exec sync

Team —

Quick summary for execs: Velox (enterprise customer, VX-ENT-4491) experienced a production SLO breach after Redwood model v3.1 (q4b-econ) rolled to their traffic on 2028-06-02 14:08 PT. Impact: sustained p99 latency spikes to ~1.2s and elevated 5xxs for ~90 minutes until Velox rolled back. Root cause under investigation; preliminary engineering hypothesis points to KV-cache churn when using q4b-econ for short prompts.

Customer ask: explanation, ETA to a fix, and credits for the impacted window. Business impact: Velox is a sizable deal (annual committed usage) and is on an activation track with Marissa's team — we should prioritize both a technical fix and a commercial response.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Rishi: confirm root cause in the next 2 hours and provide mitigation plan (pin vs serving patch).
- Monica: prep a remediation and credit offer draft (suggested: prorated credits for the incident window + technical postmortem within 48h).
- Marissa: if Velox escalates to their CRO, offer an exec sync call within 4 hours.

Please reply with availability for an incident bridge at 09:00 PT (30m).

—Jonas
